summary: Herbert Zachert was a scholar in Japanology who studied under Karl Florenz from around 1928 to 1933. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1941–1945) and the University of Bonn (circa 1960–1976).

Herman Kellgren was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Hermann Brockhaus (~1846–1848), Eugène Burnouf (~1849–1851), and Philippe-Édouard Foucaux (~1849–1851), and held a post at the University of Helsinki from 1849 to 1856.

Hermann Beckh worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kiel University (~1899–1901) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1902–1907, PhD), later holding posts at Berlin and the Prussian State Library (~1908–1921), and the Kiel Institute for the World Economy.

Hermann Berger was an Indologist and linguist who completed his doctoral and habilitation studies under Helmut Hoffmann from circa 1950 to 1956. He later held a post at Heidelberg University from 1964 to 1994.
Hermann Beythan was a scholar in the fields of Indology and linguistics. He studied under traditional teachers Ramasami Aiyar and Radscha Pillai.

Hermann Bonitz was a philosopher who studied at the University of Leipzig (~1831–1834) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1834–1836). He held posts at the University of Vienna (~1849–1867) and the Prussian Ministry of Spiritual, Educational and Medical Affairs (~1875–1888).

Hermann Brockhaus worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Bonn, the latter under August Wilhelm von Schlegel (~1828–1830). He was a professor at the University of Jena (1839) and at the University of Leipzig (~1841–1877).

Indologist and linguist Hermann Brunnhofer studied at Bonn, Berlin, Zurich, and under Albrecht Weber (~1867–1868). He held posts at several schools, the University of Oxford (~1872–1875), Aargauer Kantonsbibliothek (~1875–1888), Saint Petersburg State University (1891–1901), and the University of Bern (1901–1914).
Hermann Camillo Kellner was an Indologist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus from circa 1860 to 1864. He served as a Gymnasialprofessor at Gymnasium Zwickau from circa 1868 to 1904.

Hermann Collitz was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Göttingen, Berlin, and Halle, completing doctoral work under August Fick. He held academic posts at Bryn Mawr College (1885–1907) and Johns Hopkins University (1907–1928).
Hermann Ernst Grassmann studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1878 to 1884. He later served as a professor at the University of Giessen from circa 1904 to 1922.

Hermann Goetz worked in Indology and art history, studying at the University of Munich and under Jean Philippe Vogel. He held posts at the Kern Institute, Baroda Museum (1939–1953), National Gallery of Modern Art (1953), and Heidelberg University (1961–1976).

Hermann Grassmann worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Humboldt University of Berlin (1827–1830) under Friedrich Schleiermacher. He taught at several institutions in Stettin and Berlin, notably serving as a professor at Marienstiftsgymnasium from 1852 to 1877.

Hermann Güntert was a scholar in linguistics, Indology, and religious studies. He held academic posts at the University of Rostock from circa 1921 to 1923 and at Heidelberg University from circa 1923 to 1945.

Hermann Hirt was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Freiburg and the University of Leipzig. He served as a Privatdozent at Leipzig (1891–1912) and as a professor at the University of Giessen (1912–1936).

Hermann Hunger is a scholar of archaeology and linguistics. He studied at the universities of Vienna, Münster, and Heidelberg, and held posts at the German Archaeological Institute (~1968–1972), the University of Chicago (~1973–1976), and the University of Vienna (~1978–2007).

Hermann Hupfeld was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Marburg (~1813–1817) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1819–1822), later holding posts at Marburg (~1825–1843) and Halle-Wittenberg (~1843–1866).

Hermann Jacobi was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber and Johann Gildemeister. He held posts at the University of Bonn (1875, 1889–1922), the University of Münster (1876–1885), and Kiel University (1885).

Hermann Kulke is an historian and Indologist who studied at Madras, Freiburg, and Heidelberg, where he studied under Hermann Goetz. He held faculty posts at Heidelberg University (1967–1988) and Kiel University (1988–2003).

Hermann Oldenberg was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Göttingen and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held professorships at Humboldt University of Berlin (1878), Kiel University (1889–1908), and the University of Göttingen (1908).
